news.text: Shares fell ~6% amid AI-valuation caution and scrutiny of Palantir's UK NHS work ahead of the Aug 3 earnings print.
Nvidia AI-partnership announcement and disclosure of a Trump stake drove a 9% jump earlier in July; D.A. Davidson upgraded to Buy and Wedbush reaffirmed a $230 target.
Stock slipped further today as part of a broad growth-stock selloff, following a -3.15% pullback on July 22; no new company-specific negative news.
Goldman Sachs raised its price target to $21 (from $17) on a supportive fintech backdrop; new launches (Small Business Loans, Composer AI investing, Social 50 Income ETF) drove earlier-July gains.
Reports Q2 earnings July 29 (6 days out); Street expects continued strong revenue and profit growth.
Debt refinancing cut convertible notes from ~$47M to $16.9M and added a $30M term loan plus a $21.6M aircraft-backed facility, easing near-term liquidity.
Wheels Up signed as launch customer for Enterprise BrokerOS (up to $12M revenue); expanded Palantir SurfOS partnership; new BETA Technologies electric-aircraft demo with Hawaiian Airlines.
Risk models flag an elevated (~85%) probability of financial distress given deep losses, negative equity, and weak liquidity — still a high-risk, thinly-covered name.
Shares are down ~50% since May on AI-capex and semiconductor-volatility fears, worsened by Nvidia's exit from its equity stake in the company.
FY2026 earnings call set for July 27 (4 days out); focus will be data-center utilization, contract expansion, and capex/funding plans.
Added new operational AI capacity at Polaris Forge 1; Street stays Strong Buy (median target ~$74) despite the drawdown.
Launched 'Moving Canvas' public-art robot program (debuted at Cannes Lions) and a NoScrubs laundry-delivery pilot in LA, diversifying beyond food delivery.
Today's ~5% drop tracked a broad tech-sector selloff rather than company-specific news; Q1 revenue had risen 578% YoY to $3M but losses continue.
Board added Andreas Lieber (ex-Uber/Postmates) as a director, effective June 22.
FDA's PCAC panel (meeting July 23-24) already endorsed keeping peptide BPC-157 on the compounding-pharmacy permitted list, sending shares up double digits earlier this week.
BofA and Canaccord raised price targets to $40 on GLP-1 traction and a new $400M JPMorgan credit facility.
Stock still fell today despite the positive FDA news, swept up in the broader tech/growth-stock selloff.
Beat Q2 FY26 estimates: non-GAAP EPS $0.90 (vs. $0.86 est.), revenue $3.98B (+23.6% YoY); raised full-year subscription guidance to $15.77B.
Despite the beat-and-raise, shares fell ~3.7% today — a sell-the-news reaction amid the broader AI-capex selloff, not a fundamentals problem.
AI Control Tower and Now Assist cited as key growth drivers, with AI ACV tracking toward $1.5B by year-end.
Stock is down ~20% YTD and ~29% off its record high, lagging peers that have recovered from earlier-year selloffs.
Announced a $2.5B investment in a new 'Microsoft Frontier Co.' AI unit on July 2.
Reports fiscal Q4 results July 29 (6 days out); ~97 analysts remain Strong Buy/Buy with an average target near $590.
Shares have lost 34% YTD and 50% over 12 months as S&P downgraded Oracle's credit to BBB- on rising AI-data-center debt.
Wells Fargo maintains Buy; 43-analyst average target of $249 implies ~54% upside from current levels.
Cut 21,000 jobs to help fund a $300B OpenAI data-center commitment; market still questioning whether the AI backlog converts to cash fast enough.

A securities-fraud class action was filed after shares fell ~17% on allegations of an anticompetitive listings agreement with Redfin; a federal judge rejected a motion to dismiss the related FTC suit.
Analysts cut targets — Jefferies to $60 (from $75), KBW to $37 (from $50); stock has fallen in 3 straight sessions and is near its 52-week low.
Some analysts are floating a contrarian bull case after the ~50% 2026 selloff, but the litigation overhang remains unresolved.

Securities-fraud suit, targets cut, near lows
Balance sheet improved, new deals signed
